14.0.0.en: Joash king of Judah was followed in ascending the throne by his son Amaziah. This was in the second year of Joash the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, which was the second year of his reigning alone, because he had shared in the rule with his father Jehoahaz for about three years.

14.1.0.en: He was twenty-five years old when he took the throne, and his reign lasted twenty-nine years, the first fifteen of which coincided with the reign of Joash king of Israel, which was exactly fourteen years and a few months. The capital of his kingdom was the city of Jerusalem. The name of his mother was “Jehoaddan,” of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

14.1.1.en: We notice in the history of the kings the role of mothers in the conduct of their children. When the mothers are from Jerusalem, we rarely see the sons turning aside after false gods; but as for pagan mothers, their evil influence is clear in their sons the kings, who worshiped idols and led their peoples astray. The only exception to this is the case of the last four kings before the captivity, when the whole people had sunk low and was occupied with the worship of idols, for their mothers were from the kingdom of Judah.

14.1.2.en: In your marriage, give attention to a godly wife, who knows God and loves the Church, to secure a holy life in your home, which you and your children will enjoy, and to raise a righteous generation that rejoices the heart of God and rejoices you.

14.2.0.en: Amaziah strove to do what was right before the Lord, like Joash his father. But his righteousness did not reach what his great forefather David had reached; that is, he cared about the worship of God in His Temple, but there was some laxity, as will appear in the following verses, and he kept the Law, as appears in (vv. 5, 6).

14.3.0.en: One of the things held against him is that he let the people practice their worship of offering sacrifices and burning incense on the high places, even if it was to the true God and not to idols. All the kings from the days of Solomon fell into this error, and it encouraged some of the kings to worship idols on the high places; therefore it is considered no small error.

14.3.1.en: Do not imitate the people of the world in their habits and mix the conduct of the children of God with the conduct of the people of the world, for then Satan would have a part of your heart; for God wants you to love Him with all your heart and to walk in all your life in a way that pleases Him, and so you will receive all His blessing.

14.4.0.en: When the rule was firmly in the hand of Amaziah, he commanded the execution of the men who had killed his father, but he followed what the Law commands in this matter, which is not to kill fathers for the sins of their sons, nor to kill sons for sins committed by their fathers; every person is responsible for the sin he committed himself and is not condemned for the faults of his father or his son (Deut 24:16). This is an upright act that shows the goodness of Amaziah; for most likely some of his servants proposed to him that the sons be killed as well, as was the custom in the past among pagan peoples, to make sure that no one would rebel against him, taking vengeance for his father, but he held to the Law.

14.5.0.en: The Valley of Salt: south of the Dead Sea (the Salt Sea). Selah-Joktheel: a fortified city lying on the top of a mountain near the foot of Mount Hor. The name of the fortress of Selah today is Umm al-Bayyara.

14.5.1.en: The Edomites, whom the king had subdued, had rebelled against Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, and he fought them, as the Second Book of Chronicles mentions (2 Chr 25:5-14). So Amaziah led his army and went toward the Valley of Salt and killed ten thousand of Edom and took the city of Selah and changed its name to the name by which it remained until the writing of this book, which is Joktheel.

14.6.s.en: (2) Joash king of Israel defeats Amaziah, and then dies

14.6.0.en: After Amaziah triumphed over Edom (v. 7) he became proud, and then some soldiers from the kingdom of Israel attacked him and killed and plundered some of the inhabitants of the kingdom of Judah (2 Chr 25:5-16), and he was greatly angered and decided to make war on the kingdom of Israel, the northern kingdom, whose capital was Samaria.

14.6.1.en: And he sent to Joash to prepare himself, for he would fight him. It is clear from this that Amaziah relied on his own strength and not on God, indeed he drew away from God; for after his victory over Edom he did not glorify God, but took some of the idols of Edom and bowed down to them (2 Chr 25:14).

14.7.0.en: The thistle: a short, weak thorny plant that grows in Lebanon.

14.7.1.en: The cedar: the greatest of the trees of Lebanon; it is a strong and tall tree, indeed one of the greatest trees in the world, evergreen, and ships are made from it.

14.7.2.en: After the victory of Joash king of Israel over the Arameans (ch. 13:25) he became proud, so when Amaziah king of Judah sent to challenge him and make war on him, he was greatly angered and replied to him with a parable in which he mocks Amaziah. He compared Amaziah to the weak thistle that sent to the cedar tree asking that his son marry its daughter, as though the two were on one level, and forgot that he was a mere thistle. So he reminds Amaziah of his weakness and lowliness when compared with the king of Israel and his mighty army, which he compared to a wild beast that passed by and trampled the thistle and crushed it; that is, he reminds Amaziah of his weakness and that he cannot stand before the mighty army of Israel.

14.8.0.en: Then Joash king of Israel said in his message to Amaziah king of Judah that he had become proud after his victory over Edom and thought that he could face the army of Israel, and he advised him to keep his glory and greatness by staying at home, that is, Jerusalem, and warned him that if he fought the army of Israel he and the army of Judah would be defeated, and told him that he was doing himself harm if he attacked one stronger than himself. Joash said this with pride. It is true that the army of Israel was stronger, but it is nothing before the army of the kingdom of Assyria or the army of Egypt; but it is pride that makes a person forget himself, so that he rushes to challenge and collide with others. The purpose of the war was pride and nothing else; otherwise Amaziah would have attacked Israel suddenly to recover what they had plundered from him.

14.8.1.en: Do not rush in pride and challenge others and fall into the snares of the devil and lose the protection of God. Be humble and bear with others, even the proud among them, and God will support you and you will keep your peace.

14.9.0.en: Beth-shemesh: on the northern border of the land of Judah, twenty miles west of Jerusalem.

14.9.1.en: Amaziah did not listen to those warnings, and so the two armies met at Beth-shemesh, one of the cities of Judah. We notice that it was the army of Israel that came by the coastal road and then attacked the kingdom of Judah at the city of Beth-shemesh, which is on the road to Jerusalem, and that shows the strength of the army of Israel.

14.10.0.en: Judah was defeated before Israel and the soldiers of the army of Judah fled to their homes.

14.10.1.en: This was a punishment from God, because Judah, after their victory over Edom, worshiped the gods of Edom, as is stated in (2 Chr 25:20). The Lord is with us as long as we are with Him; if we forsake Him, He forsakes us.

14.11.0.en: The gate of Ephraim and the corner gate: they are in the northwest of the wall of Jerusalem.

14.11.1.en: Joash king of Israel, after his victory over the army of Judah, was able to seize Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-shemesh, and then took him with him to Jerusalem and broke down part of the wall of the city between the gate of Ephraim and the corner gate, so that Jerusalem would be left without protection. Joash did not intend to enter the city, for he had defeated its army and entered it easily with its king captured under his hand, but he only wanted to humiliate Jerusalem and make it weak, without walls.

14.12.0.en: Hostages: probably a group of the great men of Judah, or of the royal line. Then Joash entered Jerusalem and took all that remained in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the house of the king of gold and silver, because most of it had been given by Joash king of Judah to Hazael so that he would not make war on Jerusalem (ch. 12:18); then he took a group of the great men of Judah as hostages with him and released King Amaziah to live humbled in Jerusalem, for if he tried to rebel against Joash, Joash would kill the great men of Judah held captive by him. Then Joash returned afterward to Samaria and did not need to leave any of his army in Jerusalem, because he was confident of the weakness of Amaziah, and he also needed his army for his wars with the Arameans.

14.13.0.en: The rest of what Joash did, his excess in evil and the details of his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel, which is not the Book of Chronicles found in the Holy Bible. Then Joash died and was buried with his fathers in Samaria, and his son Jeroboam took the throne after him; he is called Jeroboam II, to distinguish him from Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the first to split the kingdom of Israel from Judah.

14.14.s.en: (3) The death of Amaziah and the reign of Azariah over Judah

14.14.0.en: The life of Amaziah extended fifteen years after the death of Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, which is exactly fourteen years and a few months, because the total period of the reign of Amaziah was twenty-nine years. The Holy Bible mentions that Amaziah lived fifteen years and does not say that he reigned, because he lived humbled, with a broken spirit, after his defeat at the hand of Joash and the taking of hostages who may have been of his own offspring and of the great men of Judah, in addition to the taking of the gold and silver, so that he became poor. And that was after his turning away from God and his bowing down to the gods of Edom, so he was defeated and humbled.

14.15.0.en: Everything connected with the acts of Amaziah is recorded in “the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.”

14.16.0.en: Lachish: a fortified city about thirty-five miles southwest of Jerusalem.

14.16.1.en: The servants of the king sensed his weakness and conspired to kill him. King Amaziah sensed this, so he left Jerusalem and fled to Lachish, but they followed him there and killed him, just as his father too had been killed in a conspiracy of his servants (ch. 12:20).

14.17.0.en: His men carried him on horses to Jerusalem, where he was buried with his fathers in the city of David.

14.17.1.en: We notice here the disgrace and contempt with which Amaziah was treated: they did not set him in a chariot like the other kings, but laid only his corpse on the horses, and then he was not buried in the tombs of the kings, but only in the city of David.

14.18.0.en: The people of Judah crowned Azariah the son of Amaziah to succeed to the throne of his father. His age at that time was sixteen years.

14.19.0.en: Elath: a town at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, near Ezion-geber, a seaport and trading port; it is modern Eilat.

14.19.1.en: Among his important works was the recovery of the city of Elath from Edom and his rebuilding of it, and that was after the death of his father Amaziah.

14.19.2.en: Thank God for His support of you and all His gifts, for He is ready to work with you beyond what you ask or think; but if you are lax in giving thanks, the devil will tempt you with the thoughts of the world and draw you away from God, so that your sense of His presence lessens and you lose His help, and then you suffer many troubles.

14.20.0.en: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Amaziah king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash became king over Israel. The capital of his kingdom was Samaria, and his rule lasted forty-one years. He was the third generation of Jehu. The reign of Jeroboam was strong, and he was the greatest of the kings of Israel in the aspects of civilization: he built houses of hewn stone and planted many vineyards and made an alliance with Assyria, and his army was strong. But his age was accompanied by spiritual decline, and the worship of idols, fornication and drunkenness spread, as is understood from the prophecies of Hosea, Joel and Amos, who were his contemporaries.

14.21.0.en: Jeroboam the son of Joash was a wicked king; he permitted the worship of idols, and evil lusts prevailed in his days, such as fornication, drunkenness and the oppression of the poor, in addition to his continuing in the worship of the idols that Jeroboam the son of Nebat had set up.

14.22.0.en: The sea of the plain: the Sea of Lot.

14.22.1.en: Jonah the son of Amittai: he is the prophet mentioned in the Book of Jonah.

14.22.2.en: Gath-hepher: it lies near Nazareth and is perhaps the present al-Mashhad, about three miles northeast of Nazareth, and in it is a tomb said to be the tomb of Jonah.

14.22.3.en: This king was able to recover a large area of land and to annex it again to the kingdom of Israel; this extended strip of land lay between the walls of the city of Hamath and the Dead Sea.

14.22.4.en: The biblical text teaches us that Jonah the prophet had already prophesied this victory, which was followed by the taking possession of these lands, but this prophecy of Jonah is not recorded in his book in the Holy Bible.

14.23.0.en: Shut up: it means children and minors.

14.23.1.en: Left: adults who move about freely and travel everywhere.

14.23.2.en: The mercy of God on His people Israel appears, although they were still in their sins, but God had pity on them by supporting Jeroboam, who was mighty, so that wars quieted in his days, that is, the kingdom of Israel was not attacked, and the people lived in freedom and tranquility; and God, by His pity, meant to call them to repentance.

14.23.3.en: God loves you even while you are in your sins and gives you many blessings, to show you His love and call you to live with Him and to leave your sins, which draw you away from Him; that is, He puts you to shame by His fatherhood and tenderness.

14.24.0.en: The Lord did not decree the blotting out of Israel and the destruction of its people, because of His longsuffering and mercy, and so He used Jeroboam the son of Joash for their deliverance. The Lord decided to bring about deliverance for His people by the hand of this king, who afterward brought wrath upon himself by continuing in evil. The patience of God with His people appears here; because the cup of the wrath of God had not yet been filled, He gives them an opportunity to return to Him, but in the end He will chastise them with captivity, that is, the killing of many and the enslaving of the rest.

14.25.0.en: Damascus: the capital of Aram, that is, present-day Syria.

14.25.1.en: Hamath, which belonged to Judah: it is the city of Hamath that is in the kingdom of Israel, that is, the northern kingdom, but it is attributed here to Judah because David subdued it and it paid tribute to him, and David was of the tribe of Judah, so it was attributed to Judah; so what is meant by Judah here is the kingdom of Israel and not the southern kingdom. The details of the war to recover the lands and all the other acts of Jeroboam and his excess in evil are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

14.26.0.en: Jeroboam died and was buried with his fathers the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah sat on the throne of Israel after him, the fourth and last generation of Jehu, and by this the word of God was fulfilled, that the descendants of Jehu would reign to the fourth generation. Azariah and Jotham kings of Judah, and Zechariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah and Pekah kings of Israel
